planting.note: Set out transplants after the last frost into well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Blue Bedder is one of the oldest seed-grown mealycup sage strains still in commerce, predating the later Victoria series.

directions: Give Blue Bedder full sun and lean, fast-draining soil; its upright, mealy-white stems carry dense violet-blue spikes from early summer through frost without deadheading. As one of the older open-pollinated seed strains of S. farinacea grown since the mid-20th century, it tends to run slightly taller and looser than modern compact bedding hybrids, so pinch young plants once to encourage branching. Treat as an annual outside zones 7-10, where the woody crown can overwinter in a mild year.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Tanzerin is a taller German-bred meadow sage selection, grown for slender, airy violet-blue spikes rather than the dense, stocky habit of Caradonna or Marcus.

directions: Site Tanzerin in lean, well-drained soil in full sun, where its looser, more open flower spikes give it a softer, more naturalistic look than the stiffly upright nemorosa cultivars bred for bedding uniformity. Shear the spent spikes back by about half once the first flush fades to push a second round of bloom into late summer. It is drought-tolerant once established and benefits from division every three to four years as the crown thins.
